stem: The graph shows Group A's antibody concentration $y$, in units per milliliter, $t$ weeks after a vaccine dose. Group B's concentration is modeled by $y = 70 - 5t$. If $(t, y)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and Group B's equation, what is the value of $y$?
stimulus: An immunologist compares two groups of volunteers. Group A received a new vaccine and their antibody levels are rising. Group B has antibodies from an earlier infection, and their levels are slowly falling.

figure.caption: Group A Antibody Concentration
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 10), (2, 20), (4, 30), (6, 40), (8, 50), and (10, 60).

explanation: Only one line is drawn, so first read its equation off the graph. It crosses the y-axis at 10 and rises 10 units for every 2 weeks, so its slope is 5 and the line is $y = 5t + 10$. The solution is the point that lies on both lines, so set the two equal: $5t + 10 = 70 - 5t$. That gives $10t = 60$, so $t = 6$. Substitute to get $y = 5(6) + 10 = 40$. Check it in Group B's equation: $70 - 5(6) = 40$.

common_errors.why: Solved for t correctly but entered the week instead of the concentration the question asks for.
Read the graphed line's y-intercept, a point on only one of the two lines, instead of the point the lines share.
Took Group B's starting value, the constant in its equation, as the solution.
Added 10 to 70 instead of subtracting it: $10t = 80$, so $t = 8$ and $y = 5(8) + 10 = 50$.

stem: The graph shows the number of folktale versions $y$ recorded in Region P after $x$ months of fieldwork. In Region Q, the number of storytellers still waiting to be interviewed is modeled by $y = 16 - x$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and the equation for Region Q, what is the value of $x + y$?
stimulus: A folklore studies team is collecting versions of a regional legend. In Region P they log each new version of the tale as they find it. In Region Q they work through a fixed list of storytellers.

figure.caption: Folktale Versions Recorded in Region P
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 4), (1, 6), (2, 8), (3, 10), (4, 12), (5, 14), and (6, 16).

explanation: Read the graphed line first. It starts at 4 and goes up 2 for every month, so it is $y = 2x + 4$. Set it equal to Region Q's equation: $2x + 4 = 16 - x$. Then $3x = 12$, so $x = 4$, and $y = 2(4) + 4 = 12$. The question asks for the sum: $x + y = 4 + 12 = 16$.

common_errors.why: Found x and stopped before adding y.
Found y and stopped before adding x.
Added the two y-intercepts, 4 + 16, which are points on one line each, instead of using the crossing point.
Dropped the $-x$ on the right side and solved $2x = 12$ to get $x = 6$. Then $y = 2(6) + 4 = 16$, and the sum is 22.

stem: The graph shows Athlete A's heart rate $y$, in beats per minute, when running at a treadmill speed of $x$ kilometers per hour. Athlete B's heart rate is modeled by $y = 15x + 40$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and Athlete B's equation, what is the value of $x$?
stimulus: A sports scientist records two athletes' heart rates during a treadmill test in which the speed is raised step by step.

figure.caption: Athlete A Heart Rate on Treadmill
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 60), (2, 80), (4, 100), (6, 120), (8, 140), (10, 160), and (12, 180).

explanation: From the graph, Athlete A's line starts at 60 and rises 20 beats for every 2 km/h, so its slope is 10 and the line is $y = 10x + 60$. Set it equal to Athlete B's equation: $10x + 60 = 15x + 40$. Subtract to get $20 = 5x$, so $x = 4$. Check: both equations give $y = 100$ when $x = 4$.

common_errors.why: Gave the y-coordinate of the solution, the heart rate, instead of the speed. This is the same as swapping the coordinates.
Read Athlete A's resting heart rate, the line's y-intercept, which is on only one of the lines.
Added the constants instead of subtracting them: $5x = 60 + 40 = 100$, so $x = 20$.
Read the slope as 20, the rise for one gridline, instead of 10 per km/h. Solving $20x + 60 = 15x + 40$ gives $x = -4$. A student who drops the sign enters 4, and one who also halves enters 2.

stem: The graph shows the water depth $y$, in centimeters, in Tide Pool 1 $x$ hours after a monitoring session began. The water depth in Tide Pool 2 is modeled by $y = 2x + 5$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and Tide Pool 2's equation, how many minutes after the session began are the two depths equal?
stimulus: A marine biologist studying sea anemones measures the water depth in two connected tide pools. As the tide goes out, Tide Pool 1 drains into Tide Pool 2.

figure.caption: Water Depth in Tide Pool 1
figure.alt: A straight decreasing line passing through (0, 30), (2, 24), (4, 18), (6, 12), (8, 6), and (10, 0).

explanation: The graphed line starts at 30 and falls 6 cm every 2 hours, so its slope is $-3$ and the line is $y = 30 - 3x$. Set it equal to Tide Pool 2's equation: $30 - 3x = 2x + 5$. Then $25 = 5x$, so $x = 5$ hours, when both depths are 15 cm. The question asks for minutes, so convert: $5 \times 60 = 300$.

common_errors.why: Solved correctly but entered the time in hours without converting it to minutes.
Entered the shared depth, the y-coordinate, instead of the time.
Read Tide Pool 1's starting depth, the y-intercept, which lies on only one line.
Added 5 to 30 instead of subtracting it: $35 = 5x$, so $x = 7$ hours, which is 420 minutes.
Read the slope as positive, $y = 3x + 30$. Solving $3x + 30 = 2x + 5$ gives $x = -25$, and a student who drops the sign and converts gets 1500.
